label: input token k
explanation: Token detector: fires on every step whose input is the letter k (original phase or copy phase, any position, any L) and essentially never otherwise (1 stray activation on a among ~6.4M dev steps; never at the delimiter step). Magnitude: in the profile examples the largest activations (~0.95-1.0 of max) are on k as the last original token right before <DEL>, and also high for k at position 0; k fed back during the copy phase activates more weakly (~0.55-0.7 of max) than the same k in the original phase. first_tok=k lift is only because those sequences contain a k. Does not fire on any other letter, digit, or <DEL>.

issues: Minor magnitude overclaim. The top-12 activations (0.95-1.0 of max) are all k at t=8, which is the last original token of an L=9 sequence. A k that is last in a short sequence is not near the peak: 'o n [k:0.67] <DEL>' (L=3) and 'b r h [k:0.67] <DEL>' (L=4). So the peak looks tied to a late absolute position (t=8 / L=9) or to k at position 0 (0.95), not to 'last original token' in general. This only concerns the magnitude notes, not the label or predicate.

The firing claims check out. by in_tok: k is active on 199034/199034 steps, every other token is ~0, and the delimiter is 0. Test misses: 2 stray activations on 'a' (0.14-0.15 of max, 0.0% of activation mass), both at step 8 directly after a k or in a k-like context, and 0 false positives. That is scattered noise, not a systematic class.
Copy phase k activations are indeed weaker (~0.55-0.72 vs 0.67-0.95 in the original phase), consistent with the claim.
